title: Visiting the Pyramids of Giza: First-Timer's Guide
excerpt: Visiting the Pyramids of Giza? Tickets cost EGP 700, gates open at 7:00, last entry 16:00. The new Visitor Centre entrance, crowd timing, interior tickets and tours from €29.
body_html:
Prices, timetables and visiting details are a November 2026 snapshot. Check the linked official pages and your departure’s current inclusions and terms before booking.

The quick answer

Visiting the Pyramids of Giza is straightforward once you know the new layout. The main entrance is now the Pyramids Visitor Centre on the Cairo to Fayoum road. The plateau opens at 7:00 with last entry at 16:00, and a foreign adult ticket costs EGP 700 (about €12). Give the site two to three hours, arrive at opening or in the late afternoon, and treat the Grand Egyptian Museum as a separate visit with its own ticket. The easiest first-timer route is a guided half-day, or a full day that pairs the pyramids with the museum.

UNESCO describes the pyramid fields from Giza to Dahshur as one World Heritage site.

Key facts

Every first Cairo trip circles back to the same question: how do you actually visit the Pyramids of Giza? The plateau has a handful of ticket types, a new entrance system and a habit of feeling overwhelming once the tour buses arrive after 9:00. This guide covers tickets, opening hours, the best route across the site, the inside-a-pyramid decision and the hassle you should expect. It is written under the name of Islam Hussein, an Egyptologist guide who has worked in Egyptian tourism since 1993; Sawa Tours (sawa.tours) is the shared-departure marketplace he founded.

How do you visit the Pyramids of Giza? The short answer

You visit the Pyramids of Giza by entering the plateau on one ticket and seeing the three pyramids, the Great Sphinx and the Panorama viewpoint inside it. You have three realistic ways in:

  1. Independently. A taxi or ride-hailing car from central Cairo reaches the Visitor Centre in about 45 minutes (longer in traffic). Set "Pyramids Visitor Centre" as the destination, as the old gate near Mena House is reported closed. You buy your own tickets and walk or ride the shuttle. Lowest cost, but no historical context, and every camel handler and photo "helper" negotiates with you directly.
  2. A guided half-day. About 4 hours. The Giza Uncovered tour includes hotel pickup, a licensed guide and the plateau entrance ticket, from €29 per person, as listed in November 2026. Meals, pyramid interiors and camel rides are not included.
  3. A guided full day with the Grand Egyptian Museum. The plateau, then Egypt's flagship museum after lunch. The Giza Pyramids, Sphinx & Grand Egyptian Museum tour runs 8 hours with an Egyptologist guide, hotel pickup, lunch and both entrance tickets included, from €71 per person, as listed in November 2026. For how the two sites fit together, read our post on the Pyramids and the Grand Egyptian Museum in one day.

The new entrance, the Visitor Centre and the shuttle

Giza's logistics changed in 2025, and many older guides are out of date. The old gate near Mena House is reported closed. The main entrance is the Pyramids Visitor Centre, south of the plateau on the Cairo to Fayoum road. It has parking, an exhibition hall and a short film (allow 20 to 30 minutes if you want them), and self-service ticket machines. Private cars and tour buses are no longer allowed onto the plateau itself: you arrive at the Visitor Centre and continue by the free electric shuttle, which is included with admission, or on foot. Guides report that visitors with limited mobility can arrange vehicle access in advance through their guide.

Guides disagree on small points, such as whether the machines take cash as well as cards, so carry a bank card and confirm on the day.

Visiting the Pyramids of Giza: tickets and opening hours

Ticket prices and hours are set by the Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities. A foreign adult pays EGP 700 for the Giza plateau, which covers the three pyramids from outside, the Great Sphinx and the Panorama area; foreign students with a valid student card pay EGP 350, and Egyptians pay EGP 60. Going inside a pyramid costs extra, and the Grand Egyptian Museum is a separate ticket at its own gate about two kilometres away.

Ticket (as of November 2026) Foreign adult
Giza plateau entry: pyramids, Sphinx, Panorama EGP 700 (about €12); student EGP 350
Great Pyramid (Khufu) interior, extra EGP 1,500 (about €25) since 1 January 2025; some Ministry pages still show EGP 1,000
Khafre or Menkaure interior, extra EGP 280 (about €5) on the Ministry list; usually only one is open
Grand Egyptian Museum, separate ticket, online only EGP 1,830 (about €31) from 1 November 2026; student or child EGP 920

Opening hours barely change through the year. The plateau opens at 7:00 and last entry is 16:00 every day; in Ramadan it opens at 8:00 with last entry at 15:30. Some sources report a 17:00 close in summer, so confirm for your date. Buy tickets at the Visitor Centre machines or in advance on the Ministry's ticketing website, egymonuments.com, and decide on any interior ticket before you arrive.

What is the best time of day to visit the Pyramids?

The best time is the first two hours after the 7:00 opening: cooler air, empty photo angles and soft desert light. The late afternoon before the 16:00 last entry is the second-best window. Midday is the slot to avoid: harsh light, peak heat and the densest crowds. Here is how a typical day on the plateau plays out:

Time Crowds and heat What it is good for
7:00 to 9:00 Fewest visitors; air still cool for most of the year Soft morning light; the eastern faces of Khufu, Khafre and Menkaure in near-quiet
9:00 to 11:00 Tour buses arrive; the shuttle stops and the Panorama viewpoint get busy Guided tours in full swing; pyramid interiors open
11:00 to 15:00 Harshest sun, biggest groups Lunch, shade, or the air-conditioned Grand Egyptian Museum instead
15:00 to 16:00 Crowds thin as day tours leave Warmer light on the limestone; last entry at 16:00
Evening Plateau closed to day visitors The sound and light show at the Sphinx is a separate ticket; check the current schedule

The one rule guides repeat most: be at the entrance for 7:00. You get cool air, clear photo angles and an hour with the pyramids nearly to yourself, then you can finish in the museum's air-conditioning while the tour buses circle the plateau.

Season matters as much as the clock. October to April brings the mild weather most travellers want. From May to September the plateau can pass 35°C (95°F) by midday, so a summer visit means opening time or nothing. Winter mornings can be genuinely cold before 9:00, so carry a light layer from November to February.

The best first-timer route across the Giza plateau

The classic first-timer loop runs: the three pyramids first, then the Panorama viewpoint, then the Great Sphinx and Khafre's Valley Temple. The Giza Uncovered tour follows the same shape, with hotel pickup included:

  1. Hotel pickup. From your Cairo or Giza hotel, with a short briefing from your guide.
  2. The three pyramids. Khufu's Great Pyramid, about 139 metres tall today and about 4,500 years old; then Khafre's, which looks taller thanks to its higher ground and the casing stones still clinging to its summit; then Menkaure's, the smallest of the three.
  3. Panorama viewpoint. The high ground southwest of the pyramids where all three line up for the classic group photo. Camel and horse handlers work here; Sawa does not sell or arrange rides, so if you want one, agree the price and duration before you mount, or simply decline.
  4. Optional pyramid interior. An extra ticket, paid separately. The Great Pyramid demands a head for steep, low tunnels.
  5. Great Sphinx and Valley Temple. The lion-bodied Sphinx faces east, and its neighbouring temples were built of limestone quarried on the plateau.
  6. Back to your hotel, after about 4 hours in all.

Should you go inside a pyramid?

Going inside a pyramid is a hot, crouched climb to a bare granite chamber: worth doing once for the experience, not for anything on display. The Great Pyramid of Khufu is the most impressive and the most demanding: a steep ascending passage, then the Grand Gallery, then the King's Chamber. The Khafre and Menkaure interiors are shorter and cost far less. Interior tickets are separate from plateau entry. If you are claustrophobic, skip it: the passages are low and narrow enough that most adults walk bent over. Many travellers prefer to spend the money on the museum instead.

How to avoid touts at the Pyramids of Giza

Touts at Giza are persistent but manageable, and nearly every hassle starts the same way: someone offers a service you did not ask for, such as a photo, a camel or a "shortcut" past a closed gate. A calm "la, shukran" (no, thank you) works better than a long conversation, and the licensed guide on your departure absorbs most of it for you.

  • The "closed" line. Real tickets come from the Visitor Centre machines or the Ministry's website. Anyone claiming the site is closed and offering an alternative is redirecting you to something they earn from.
  • Camel and horse pricing. Sawa does not sell or arrange rides. If you take one, agree the total, the duration and the route before mounting, and ask whether the quote is per person or per animal.
  • Unsolicited "guidance". A man offering to shoot your photo at the Panorama viewpoint or show you a "secret" angle expects baksheesh (a tip). If you did not ask, you owe nothing.
  • The "you cannot walk here" claim. The plateau is walkable, and the shuttle is free. Some operators simply prefer you not to know it.

Half day at Giza or a full day with the Grand Egyptian Museum?

Choose by energy, not interest: the plateau alone is a half-day, and the plateau plus the Grand Egyptian Museum (GEM) is a full day that suits most first-timers in the cool season. The GEM opened fully in November 2025, about two kilometres from the pyramids, and holds more than 100,000 artefacts, including the complete Tutankhamun collection of more than 5,000 objects and Khufu's boats. Its galleries are open 9:00 to 18:00, and until 21:00 on Wednesdays and Saturdays; tickets are sold online only, at tickets.gem.eg. On a short layover or in high summer, the half day at opening time beats a rushed marathon.

The verdict on visiting the Pyramids of Giza

A good first visit comes down to three decisions: arrive at the 7:00 opening or in the late afternoon, budget EGP 700 plus any interior tickets, and choose between ending your day at the Sphinx or at the Grand Egyptian Museum. On a first trip in the cool season, the full day wins. Next step: browse forming Giza departures on Sawa, or start your own date on the Giza Pyramids, Sphinx & GEM tour. Reserving a seat is free.

faq.q: Can I visit the Pyramids of Giza without a tour?
faq.a: Yes. Taxis and ride-hailing cars reach the Visitor Centre from central Cairo in roughly 45 minutes, and you can buy the EGP 700 foreign adult ticket from the machines there or on the Ministry's website. The trade-off is context and hassle: no one explains what you are seeing, and every camel handler and photo "helper" negotiates with you directly. A guide is not compulsory, but most first-timers find one pays for itself in time saved.

faq.q: How much time do you need at the Pyramids of Giza?
faq.a: Two to three hours covers the plateau itself: the three pyramids, the Panorama viewpoint and the Great Sphinx. Add about 45 minutes if you enter one pyramid, and several more hours for the Grand Egyptian Museum. In practice that means a half-day for the pyramids alone, or a full day when the museum is included.

faq.q: Is it safe to visit the Pyramids of Giza?
faq.a: Yes, with normal city precautions. The plateau is a guarded, ticketed archaeological site with security at the entrance and tourist police on duty, and violent crime against visitors is rare. The realistic risk is being overcharged for a camel ride or a photo, not your physical safety. Solo travellers who would rather not go alone can join a Sawa shared departure of up to eight travellers.

faq.q: What should I wear to visit the pyramids?
faq.a: Cover shoulders and knees, wear closed shoes with grip for the plateau's rock and gravel, and bring a hat, sunglasses and sunscreen in every season; the site has almost no shade. In winter mornings, add a light layer you can drop by 10:00. In summer, a refillable water bottle matters more than any outfit rule, and pyramid interiors stay hot even in cool months.

faq.q: What happens if my Sawa departure doesn't fill?
faq.a: Nothing is charged. A date confirms when four travellers have reserved it, and until then no card is charged or held. If it has not reached four seven days before the tour, it is cancelled, nothing is charged, and another date is suggested, or you can start your own. Once a date is confirmed, it runs even if one traveller later drops out.

faq.q: Can you see the pyramids for free?
faq.a: Only from outside the site. The plateau is a ticketed archaeological site, so the pyramids, the Sphinx and the Panorama viewpoint all sit behind the EGP 700 ticket for foreign visitors. There is no free general entry.
